confirmed_defects_fixed: Outlier z-score threshold accepted zero, negative, NaN and infinite values; it now requires a finite positive threshold.
Supplied CompaRatio could imply a non-finite BandMidpoint; non-finite derived midpoints now fail closed as unavailable.
Gender pay-gap minimum group size accepted negative, zero, fractional, NaN and infinite values; it now requires a finite integer of at least two.
Raw gender pay-gap percentage did not disclose its reference denominator; output now declares male_mean_salary explicitly.
Unknown/unmapped gender rows were silently excluded; output now reports known binary-gender population, excluded count and coverage.

Welch inference on extreme finite salaries could overflow inside SciPy; a scale-invariant stable Welch implementation now avoids non-finite intermediate arithmetic and fails closed when inference is undefined.
analyze_all exposed employee-level salary outlier records internally; it now returns aggregate outlier counts only.
External BandMidpoint values were ignored when CompaRatio was absent; supplied market-band midpoint is now the authoritative compa-ratio basis.
Contradictory supplied BandMidpoint and CompaRatio values were trusted independently; they are now reconciled row by row and inconsistent rows fail closed.
Ineligible small job-title gender strata exposed exact male/female counts; suppressed strata now hide exact subgroup counts and disclose only the minimum support rule.
Overall unsupported male/female comparisons could expose exact undersized group counts; unsupported small groups are now count-suppressed.

Direct salary statistics in department dispersion, outlier z-scores, percentiles, tenure summaries and salary-attrition association were hardened against extreme finite magnitudes using scale-stable arithmetic.
boundaries: Current compensation summaries use current active employees with valid positive salary.
EquityScore is a compatibility field for salary-dispersion consistency, not an adjusted pay-equity conclusion.
Department-median compa values are an explicit compatibility fallback, not formal market compa-ratios.
Formal compa-ratio semantics require a supplied valid BandMidpoint or a supplied ratio that can be reconciled to a finite midpoint.
Gender pay-gap results are descriptive disparity indicators and not legal, causal or regression-adjusted pay-equity determinations.
Small gender strata are suppressed rather than exposing exact subgroup counts.
Employee-level salary outlier records are not exposed through the aggregate analysis surface or governed API.
readiness_boundary: This cycle materially strengthens confidence in deterministic compensation calculations, finite numerical behavior, population accounting, compa semantics, disparity-screening transparency and privacy suppression. It does not establish organization-specific legal pay equity or market competitiveness without validated external compensation bands and appropriate covariates.
